curated.instructions: omr/instructions/42064-1-1.pdf (bag 1 builds the helicopter and the submarine, bags 2-3 the ship, steps up to 256; pages 202-203 show every function, with the knobs on the bridge roof marked A and B and the knob behind the bridge marked C)

functions.does: Knob A, the left of the two black gears on the bridge roof, raises and lowers the crane's yellow boom: its shaft runs down through a universal joint and bevel gears to a shaft under the deck, back to the crane, and up through the turntable's middle to a worm, which turns a 24 tooth gear on the boom's pivot.
functions.source: book: pages 202-203 (the bridge roof picture with knobs A and B; the crane drawn at three heights, with the arrow at the gear on its pivot marked A)

functions.does: Knob B, the right of the two black gears on the bridge roof, slews the crane round on its turntable: its shaft runs down through a universal joint and bevel gears to three 16 tooth gears under the deck and a shaft back to the crane, where a 12 tooth gear turns the turntable.
functions.source: book: pages 202-203 (the bridge roof picture with knob B; the crane picture marked B, with the arrow round its base)

functions.does: Knob C, the gear behind the bridge, steers the ship: its upright shaft turns a long shaft under the deck that runs back to the stern, where cranks on it swing the two rudders together and turn the rear wheel bogie the ship rolls on.
functions.source: book: pages 202-203 (knob C on the bridge picture; the picture marked C shows the ship turning); what the shaft moves at the stern is read from the model
functions.note: unsure which way the book means the ship to steer: the picture marked C draws arrows at the bow; the rudders p17 and p18 and the bogie p33 are read from the model

functions.does: The ship rolls on hidden wheels under its hull: a single wheel under the bow, a pair in the middle, and a pair on a bogie at the stern.
functions.source: book: page 201 (the finished ship, the wheels visible under the hull); inferred from the model

functions.does: The helicopter's black gear under the rotor mast turns the main rotor, and through a pair of 12 tooth gears and a bevel gear pair a shaft back to the tail turns the tail rotor.
functions.source: book: bag 1 steps 11-14 and 22 (the rotor mast with its gear below), pages 202-203 (the helicopter picture with the arrow at the gear under it)

functions.does: The submarine's rear knob on top turns its two propellers: a bevel gear pair takes the knob's turn down to a 20 tooth gear, which turns a 12 tooth gear on each propeller shaft.
functions.source: book: bag 1 sub steps 4-10 (the propeller gears), pages 202-203 (the submarine seen from behind with the arrow on its knob)

functions.does: The submarine's front knob on top swings its two arms with their grabbers out and in: the knob turns a worm, which turns a 24 tooth gear between two knob gears, each of which turns an arm's knob gear.
functions.source: book: bag 1 sub steps 8-24 (the worm, the 24 tooth gear and the arms), pages 202-203 (the submarine from the front with the arrow on its knob and the arms swinging)

functions.does: The hook block hangs from the crane's boom tip, for lifting the submarine.
functions.source: book: steps 253-254, pages 202-203 (the submarine hanging from the crane)
functions.note: the function pages show no winch; the submarine seems to be hung on the hook by hand

functions.does: The hatch on the foredeck, in front of the bridge, lifts open.
functions.source: inferred: the hatch submodel sits on its own pins in the model; the book's function pages don't show it
functions.note: unsure whether the hatch is meant to open

questions.question: Does knob C steer the rudders and the rear bogie?
